tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when a pipeline or training run registers no model package version...'), focuses on user-facing symptoms rather than implementation details, explicitly lists many trigger contexts (unregistered models, unapproved deploys, rejected instance types, slow lineage queries, MLflow errors, cross-account sharing, etc.), and notes it applies even when the user doesn't name the domain directly. It is a dense but single paragraph, which is reasonably concise given the breadth of triggers it must cover.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when a pipeline or training run registers no model package version, production deploys are not gated on approval status, a served model has no registered or approved package behind it... even if they do not mention approval status, RegisterModel steps, resource policies, supported instance types, MLflow versions or CMK encryption by name.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body avoids explaining general concepts (e.g., it doesn't explain what SageMaker Model Registry is or basic AWS concepts) and jumps directly into domain-specific checks, routing logic, and governance procedures that the agent wouldn't otherwise know.
tests.evidence: "You review the SageMaker Model Registry governance of a customized or fine-tuned GenAI artifact — the lineage and approval governance for the output of a SageMaker training/customization job."

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The body contains a compact index table of check-ids with one-line descriptions, and the detailed rules, remediations, and citations are explicitly deferred to references/checks-sagemaker-model-registry.md rather than embedded in the body.
tests.evidence: "The full six-column detection rules, remediations, and citations live in the reference — the table below is a what-it-catches index."

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All five files in references/ are linked via markdown links in the body.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link in the body is paired with a clear condition for when to load it, e.g. router rows and appendix entries specify trigger conditions.
tests.evidence: "load it before assigning any check-id or severity" and "load it when a symptom matches a row below" for checks-sagemaker-model-registry.md

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths rooted at references/ with no absolute paths or traversal.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (read-only posture, severity assignment, account ID masking) are given exact, non-negotiable rules, while flexible areas (e.g., how to investigate a symptom) explain purpose and let the agent reason about which API to call.
tests.evidence: "Never call a registry mutation (CreateModelPackage, UpdateModelPackage) or any other mutating API." versus "Match the symptom, confirm with the collection calls, then report with the check-id and severity from the catalog."

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The Router table designates a clear 'First read' API call per symptom rather than listing multiple equal options, establishing defaults for investigation steps.
tests.evidence: "Our fine-tuned model isn't in the registry, it was never registered | ListModelPackages for the artifact's S3 location"

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable approach (symptom matching, check catalog, review procedure, validation gate) rather than declaring a one-off task, while still including specific templates and constraints appropriately.
tests.evidence: "Match the symptom, confirm with the collection calls, then report with the check-id and severity from the catalog."

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill includes a dedicated 'Common wrong answers' section documenting non-obvious pitfalls specific to this domain, functioning as a gotchas section.
tests.evidence: "'There is an Approved package in the group, so the group is governed.' Approval only counts for the version that is actually deployed or staged."
